# Install the Terraform policy CLI

The Terraform policy command-line interface, `tfpolicy`, tests and validates policies locally. Testing your policies helps you to identify errors when you write and update your policies, before you enforce them against your Terraform workspaces. Install the `tfpolicy` command on your local system before you author your policies and policy tests.

@include "beta.mdx"

## Prerequisites

Terraform policy requires Terraform v1.16 or later.

## Installation

HashiCorp distributes the Terraform policy CLI as an executable binary that you can install on supported operating systems, including Microsoft Windows, macOS, and several Linux distributions.

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="Manual installation">

To install `tfpolicy`, visit the [HashiCorp releases website](https://releases.hashicorp.com/tfpolicy/) to download the appropriate binary for your operating system as a zip archive.

After you download `tfpolicy`, unzip the archive.

Finally, make sure that the `tfpolicy` binary is available in a directory that is in your system's `PATH`. 

Every build of `tfpolicy` includes a `SHA256SUMS` and a `SHA256SUMS.sig` file to validate your downloaded binary. Refer to the [verify HashiCorp binary downloads tutorial](https://developer.hashicorp.com/well-architected-framework/operational-excellence/verify-hashicorp-binary) for more information.

</Tab>

<Tab heading="Homebrew on macOS">

[Homebrew](https://brew.sh/) is a free and open-source package management system for macOS. You can install the official [Hashicorp tap](https://github.com/hashicorp/homebrew-tap) and then tfpolicy from your terminal.

First, install the HashiCorp tap, a repository of all our Homebrew packages.

```shell-session
$ brew tap hashicorp/tap
```

Now, install `tfpolicy` with the `hashicorp/tap/tfpolicy` formula.

```shell-session
$ brew install hashicorp/tap/tfpolicy
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

## Verify installation

Verify that the installation worked by opening a new terminal and using the `--help` flag of `tfpolicy`:

```shell-session
$ tfpolicy --help
Usage: tfpolicy [--version] [--help] <command> [<args>]

Available commands are:
    test        Test Terraform Policy files.
    validate    Validate Terraform policies configuration files.
    version     Prints the tfpolicy version
```

## Usage

To begin writing policies, refer to [Terraform policy - Write policies](/terraform/policy/write).

## Reference

The tfpolicy CLI provides the following commands:

- [`tfpolicy test`](/terraform/policy/reference/cli/test): Run policy tests.
- [`tfpolicy validate`](/terraform/policy/reference/cli/validate): Validate policy syntax.
- [`tfpolicy version`](/terraform/policy/reference/cli/version): Print out Terraform policy CLI version.
